correctness.rationale: The only two possible third edges between a disjoint pair of biclique edges are its cross-edges. Both are absent exactly for the transposed pair across two distinct deleted matching edges. A third packing edge could neither be disjoint from nor meet both such selected edges. All remaining packings with at least two edges are pairwise incident; in a bipartite graph this means a single star with unique center. Counting star k-subsets using precise degree multiplicities, adding binomial(t,2) crossed pairs for k=2, and treating singletons and empty set separately proves every coefficient for all m,n>=2 and 0<=t<=min(m,n). Executed verifier checks 144444 subsets in 32 small cases, 1048576 subsets for H_5,5,5, and 5062 pairwise predicate comparisons, without using finite enumeration as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 defining paper proves only maximum edge-open packing cardinalities for complete multipartite graphs (Proposition 2.3), not the size profile after matching deletion. A 2024 edge-deletion theorem bounds maximum cardinality, and a separate 2024 graph-product paper bounds maximum packing numbers without this enumerator. The 2019 injective-edge-coloring induced-star-forest equivalence does not count or identify the binomial(t,2) exceptional non-star pairs. The new contribution is the complete exact coefficient law for all admissible m,n,t; originality remains provisional against unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The family K_{m,n} minus a matching is a canonical dense-to-crown interpolation; EOP sets are exact admissible single color classes in injective edge coloring. Earlier studies concentrated on maximum cardinality or coloring index, whereas the new structural theorem classifies every EOP set and counts each cardinality for arbitrary unequal sides. The exceptional binomial(t,2) crossed pairs identify the complete new non-star phenomenon caused by the missing matching, providing a natural full combinatorial invariant with reproducible exact coefficient profile. This is a classification/count, not merely a renamed known scalar or an arbitrary small case.
